newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia fishermen said enjoying Australian jails.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia fishermen said enjoying Australian jails.

text.p: Indonesian fisherman are deliberately violating Australia's maritime borders because they apparently enjoy doing time in Australian jails, the navy chief said.

"I am concerned about conditions like this because it appears fishermen in fact feel happy if they cross the border and enter Australian waters and are detained by our neighbour's navy," Naval Chief of Staff Vice-Admiral Arief Koesharjadi said.
Koesharjadi, speaking in Ambon in eastern Indonesia, said the fisherman were also happy because when they were eventaully sent home, they got to ride in an aeroplane.
"In fact, in jail they feel very comfortable as they are given food, clothes and given pocket money if they work," he said.
The fishermen gave various excuses when caught such as their sails ripped or their engine broke down when they were detained by the Australian navy, he added.
Koesharjadi called on fishermen working areas near the sea boundary to be equipped with sufficient navigational instruments so they do cross into Australian territory.
